transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-27
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Marcus Reed (Oxford Head of Security), Elena Soto (Oxford DevOps), Tom Wang (Product), Anika Patel (Legal)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in to review security/compliance items during pilot. Focus on SSO, audit logs, retention, SOC 2.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining for the weekly sec sync. uh quick roll call?
[00:08] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:09] Elena: Elena here.
[00:11] Tom: Tom, yep.
[00:13] Anika: Anika from legal.
[00:15] Jordan: great, and priya from our side?
[00:17] Priya: Yup, hi all. i'm the SE on the pilot.

[02:05] Jordan: Quick agenda — SSO status, audit logs/export, retention policies, SOC2 materials, and then any blockers for the dedicated bench. Marcus, do you want to start with SSO?
[02:20] Marcus: Sure. So we tried the SSO link you sent last week, we hit a couple of issues — the IdP response had an attribute mismatch. i think the saml name id was different than what your connector expects. also, we need to know if we can map groups to RBAC roles in the console.
[02:50] Priya: Yeah, that matches what we saw in the test logs — the attribute name comes through as 'mail' instead of 'email'. our connector has a mapping table, we can accept either, but we need the SAML metadata from your IdP to set it up. we support group mappings to roles, and you can configure those mappings via the Redwood Console (dashboard) or via API.
[03:20] Elena: okay we'll share the metadata. also curious — in the private deployment is the SSO termination on-prem or at the control plane? meaning, will auth traffic leave our VPC?
[03:37] Priya: Good question. For Private (VPC) option, SSO/SAML assertions are exchanged within the customer's network — the control plane can be customer-managed. if you pick Dedicated hosted in our cloud, the control plane handles it and you get SAML assertions to our auth endpoint over TLS. for strict customers we recommend Private with customer-managed control plane so nothing traverses public internet beyond your own network. note: terminology in the pilot deck might say 'private control plane' — apologies if that caused confusion.
[04:10] Marcus: That helps. Legal will want that in writing — Anika can you note that?
[04:15] Anika: yes noted, we'll need an architecture diagram and where the assertion flow stops.

[06:00] Jordan: Next — audit logs. Priya, can you explain the log coverage and what format the export is?
[06:08] Priya: Sure. Redwood emits structured audit events for token usage, model route, request/response metadata (redacted where configured), admin activity (user creation, role changes), and API key lifecycle events. Exports are available in JSON lines (ndjson) and can be pushed to S3, or streamed to your SIEM via our syslog / cloudwatch forwarder. We also have a sample CSV if you prefer that for quick inspection.
[06:45] Marcus: Does the audit log include request payloads or are those redacted by default?
[06:50] Priya: Payloads are redacted by default — we include metadata about the request (size, model, token counts, route id) and a hash of the prompt for traceability. If you need full payload capture for an internal bench, we can enable a secure, ephemeral capture — but that requires additional compliance signoff and storage controls.
[07:15] Elena: For our regulator we need 12 months of logs, and a way to export on-demand. Can Redwood support retention that long?
[07:23] Priya: Yes — retention is configurable per-account; hosted defaults are shorter (90 days) but Dedicated/Private can be set to 12 months or longer in the retention policy. We recommend retention + tiered archival to S3 Glacier for older logs. We'll share a retention template.
[07:40] Marcus: Also need immutability — WORM-like storage. is that supported?
[07:46] Priya: We support write-once configurations if logs are exported to your S3 bucket with object lock enabled; Redwood's export pipeline will respect bucket-level settings. If you want server-side immutability in our hosted offering, that's a product ask — currently the pattern is to export to your controlled storage for WORM compliance.

[09:30] Tom: curious — what about PII in logs? you mentioned hashes, but can we set masking/anonymization rules?
[09:39] Priya: Yes. We provide configurable redaction rules. By default we strip obvious PII fields and replace them with deterministic token hashes. For higher assurance we can run a prompt/response filter that removes or masks free text. That filtering can be applied inline or as part of the export pipeline.
[10:00] Marcus: good. Next — SOC 2. Jordan, you said you would share the SOC 2 Type II?
[10:06] Jordan: yes, we will. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II — i'll share the report and our security whitepaper. note that some customer-specific scoping details are redacted in the public report, we can provide an SOC 2 letter of attestation and point you to control mappings.
[10:30] Anika: we'll need control mappings for encryption-at-rest, key management, incident response, and vendor access.
[10:37] Jordan: got it. the pack we'll send includes a controls matrix mapping to your standard (they have a template) and KMS docs. For private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations — we documented both AWS KMS and HSM patterns.
[10:55] Marcus: on KMS — can we bring our own key and have Redwood never see plaintext?
[11:00] Priya: Yes, in Private we support BYOK where the key is in your KMS and Redwood's worker processes perform encrypt/decrypt in an enclave or in your VPC depending on deployment. For hosted we have envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via cross-account KMS, but there are tradeoffs; we'll include a diagram.
[11:20] Elena: does that affect latency for the bench?
[11:24] Priya: Minimal — initial handshake/KMS calls are per-session. For heavy token throughput we cache decrypted keys in memory only with strict lifetime and rotation. We'll include expected latency delta in the KB.

[13:50] Jordan: Bench plan — customer wants a 10k-token run in a dedicated pool to validate auditability and perf. Are we aligned to schedule that?
[13:58] Marcus: yes, we'd like that. also want the log capture during bench to include token counts and route ids.
[14:06] Priya: we can set up a dedicated pool for that window and enable ephemeral full-payload capture to a secured S3 bucket for your team to analyze. note capture requires extra signoff because of payload storage.
[14:25] Tom: And cost? approximate estimate for a one-hour dedicated run?
[14:29] Jordan: I'll send a rough cost estimate in the follow-up; it depends on the instance type. we can give a per-hour estimate and a short-run promo credit for the POC.

[15:45] Marcus: Another question — audit trails for admin actions. We need a chain-of-custody for role changes. Does the Console log who approved what and the IP address?
[15:55] Priya: Yes, admin events include user id, actor ip, timestamp, action type, and changeset. All included in the audit export. For higher-fidelity traceability you can turn on session recording for the Console (captures UI actions) — again that's optional and subject to retention policy.

[17:10] Anika: Regarding legal / data residency: our legal team needs to know where backups and logs are stored physically for hosted vs private.
[17:20] Jordan: Hosted is region-specific — we support NA/EU regions, and backups stay in-region by default. Private keeps everything in your environment. We'll send a region-by-region data residency summary.

[18:50] Elena: On encryption rotation — what's the rotation cadence for keys in hosted?
[18:55] Priya: Hosted uses a managed rotation cadence of 90 days for service keys; customer-managed keys are on the cadence you control. For envelope encryption we rotate data encryption keys more frequently and rewrap using the master key. We'll include rotation docs.

[21:00] Marcus: Two compliance asks — we need pen test reports and vulnerability management cadence.
[21:08] Jordan: We run yearly third-party pen tests and internal scans quarterly. we'll share redacted pen test summary and vuln mgmt policy. Full detail accessible under an NDA if needed.

[22:30] Tom: small thing — in the console our team couldn't find where to set retention for logs. walk us through?
[22:36] Priya: Sure. under Settings -> Compliance -> Audit & Retention there's a dropdown to set retention window and a toggle to export to external storage. i can screen-share later or send a short clip.

[24:00] Marcus: any blockers from Redwood side to doing the bench next week?
[24:05] Priya: Need your SAML metadata and confirmation of the S3 bucket (or we can use our temporary secure bucket). Also need signoff to enable ephemeral payload capture for that bench.
[24:20] Elena: we'll provide SAML metadata and create an S3 bucket with object lock enabled.

[26:00] Anika: legal will want the DPA + data flow diagram before payload capture.
[26:06] Jordan: yes, we'll attach DPA and a dataflow diagram in the pack.

[28:30] Jordan: quick recap of decisions: 1) Customer to send SAML metadata and test user; 2) Redwood to send SOC2 artifacts, pen test summary, and retention template; 3) Set up dedicated bench once S3 + SAML are done.
[28:50] Marcus: sounds right.

[30:15] Priya: I'll also include examples of the audit log ndjson export and a sample parser script so you can ingest into your SIEM quickly.

[32:00] Jordan: Any other legal / policy things?
[32:07] Anika: just the DPA + a brief on subcontractor access — who will have access to logs in hosted environment?
[32:15] Jordan: Access limited to ops on a need-to-know; subcontractors are listed in our SOC 2. We'll include a subcontractor access list.

[34:40] Marcus: Last question — isolation for dedicated pool: is it single-tenant network and GPU level?
[34:48] Priya: Dedicated pools are single-tenant at the node level; networking can be VPC-peered or private link. GPUs are dedicated for your pool, and we avoid colocating other customers on those nodes. We'll include an architecture note.

[36:10] Tom: Great. Let's confirm dates — Jordan you'll send the security pack by Friday?
[36:15] Jordan: Yes, by 2026-05-30. Priya, logs sample by Tuesday?
[36:20] Priya: I will deliver by 2026-06-02.
[36:25] Elena: We'll provide SAML metadata and S3 info by 2026-06-04.

[38:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with an email including the SOC 2, DPA, retention template, and bench scheduling link.
[38:08] Marcus: thanks all.
[38:10] Anika: thanks.
[38:12] Tom: bye.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., 'K-V cash' for KV cache in early internal notes), filler 'uh' and 'you know' retained. Links referenced: SOC2 report (link sent in follow-up), retention template (to be attached), bench scheduling sheet (link in email).
